players.product: Atlas and Origin agentic target-to-antibody discovery platform

quarterly_data.signal: Atlas is an agentic target-to-lead system integrating literature, genetics and single-cell sequencing data; targets flow into Origin for epitope-specific de novo antibody design and then into in-house wet-lab validation. Atlas independently recovered genetic evidence linking prolactin biology to pattern hair loss and endometriosis.

Origin model improvements reduce the library size needed to identify high-quality leads by 1,000x. Absci's first programs reached IND-enabling studies in under 2.5 years and for under $15 million total cost, and management expects Atlas plus newer Origin models to improve those metrics further.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,000x smaller libraries; <2.5 years and <$15M to IND-enabling

quarterly_data.signal: ABS-201 interim pharmacokinetics showed an estimated half-life of at least 65 days, supporting two or three doses over six months and modeled receptor occupancy above 90%. The company targets an interim 13-week proof-of-concept readout in H2 2026 and full 26-week data in early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: half-life >=65 days; 2-3 doses/6 months; >90% modeled occupancy

quarterly_data.signal: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $201.1 million after a $100 million financing, supporting operating runway into H2 2028. Q2 R&D expense was $22.6 million as internal clinical programs advanced.

contracts.signal: Eli Lilly made a $40 million strategic investment within Absci's $100 million financing and is collaborating on ABS-201's clinical-development strategy, including a Lilly representative joining the endometriosis advisory board. Lilly received no rights to ABS-201.
